walkthrough:
Interpret the first inequality $|z - 3 - \mathrm{i}| \leqslant 3$:
This can be written as $|z - (3 + \mathrm{i})| \leqslant 3$, which represents the circular disc of radius $3$ centred at the point $(3, 1)$ (representing the complex number $3 + \mathrm{i}$).

Interpret the second inequality $|z| \geqslant |z - 4\mathrm{i}|$:
$|z| = |z - 0|$ represents the distance from the origin $(0, 0)$, while $|z - 4\mathrm{i}|$ represents the distance from the point $(0, 4)$.
The boundary $|z| = |z - 4\mathrm{i}|$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment from $(0, 0)$ to $(0, 4)$, which is the horizontal line $y = 2$.
The condition $|z| \geqslant |z - 4\mathrm{i}|$ requires points to be closer to $(0, 4)$ than to $(0, 0)$, so $y \geqslant 2$.

Combine the two geometric conditions:
The region consists of all points lying inside or on the circle with centre $(3, 1)$ and radius $3$, and on or above the horizontal line $y = 2$.

Sketch and shade the region:
Draw the circle $(x - 3)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 9$ and the horizontal line $y = 2$ as solid boundaries, and shade the upper circular segment lying above $y = 2$ within the circle.
